title: How does a write reach the disk?
question: A write is in memory until it is written back. fsync() makes it durable now: what does that take?
text: Call 3, [fsync(fd)](3): [ext4_sync_file](3:ext4_sync_file) Now the data must reach the disk. [ext4_mb_new_blocks](3:ext4_mb_new_blocks) Write the dirty page back: now a block is chosen for it, by the multiblock allocator, from the block bitmap. [jbd2_journal_commit_transaction](3:jbd2_journal_commit_transaction:any) The journal (jbd2, its own thread) commits the metadata changes: the bitmaps, the inode, the directory block. [submit_bio](3:submit_bio) The block layer: an I/O request to the disk, /dev/loop0, whose blocks are a file in memory.
